title: A real-world abstraction example
answer: A real-world abstraction is a control panel or remote: the user presses a clear operation such as start, stop, or move without needing to know the motor-control electronics, communication protocol, or internal algorithm. In software, an interface can represent that visible control surface while concrete implementations hide device-specific details.
